stem.en: A dolphin lives in water and swims as a fish does. Why does it belong to the mammals?

text.en: Fins are found only on mammals.

feedback.en: Fish have fins too, so fins cannot mark a mammal.

text.en: Any swimmer longer than one metre is a mammal.

feedback.en: Length does not decide a group. Some fish are far longer than a dolphin.

text.en: It has mammary glands and breathes with lungs.

feedback.en: Right. Mammary glands and lungs place it with the mammals. Swimming does not give it gills.

text.en: Where an animal lives always decides its group.

feedback.en: A dolphin and a fish share the water but belong to different groups, so habitat does not decide.

explanation.en: A dolphin mother has mammary glands and feeds her calf on milk, and a dolphin breathes air with lungs. A tiger shares these features. Living in water gives a dolphin no gills, so it is a mammal that swims well.

hints.en: Think about how a dolphin breathes and how it feeds its young.
